name: shader-text-reveal
title: Text Reveal
description: Words appear one at a time: a flowing, halftone-textured light material fills the letters, then clears to clean white type before a dark wave removes the word. Drawn in WebGL over a transparent background.
useWhen: A short headline needs a shader reveal, one word at a time.
The material should appear inside letters before they settle into white.
avoidWhen: A quiet text entrance is enough: use soft-blur-in.
Words should physically morph into each other: use kinetic-morph-text.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Text
variables.description: Words appear one at a time. Separate phrases with new lines to keep them together.

variables.label: Font size
variables.description: Largest type size, for a 720-pixel-tall frame; it scales with the frame and shrinks to fit the width.

variables.label: Font
variables.description: CSS font family for the type.

variables.label: Frames per word
variables.description: Frames each word takes, including its entrance and exit. The final word stays.

variables.label: Shader strength
variables.description: Strength of the shader material inside the letters, 0 to 1.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Lower renders much faster: the light field is costly to draw in software.
